title: MHT-CET 2025 (PCM) — 19 April 2025, Shift II
description: MHT-CET 2025 PCM paper (19 April 2025, Shift II): Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, 150 questions. Questions from the Target Publications paper; answers and explanations are worked out by AI (no official key), so double-check any that look off.
instructions: This question booklet contains 150 Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs). Section-A: Physics & Chemistry - 50 Questions each; Section-B: Mathematics - 50 Questions.
Choice and sequence for attempting questions will be as per the convenience of the candidate.
Determine the one correct answer out of the four available options given for each question.
Each question with correct response shall be awarded one (1) mark. There shall be no negative marking.

questions.text: The resultant of two vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is $\vec{C}$. If the magnitude of $\vec{B}$ is doubled, the new resultant vector becomes perpendicular to $\vec{A}$, then the magnitude of $\vec{C}$ is
questions.explanation:
New resultant $\vec{A}+2\vec{B} \perp \vec{A}$: $A^2 + 2\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = 0 \Rightarrow \vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = -\frac{A^2}{2}$.
$C^2 = A^2 + B^2 + 2\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = A^2 + B^2 - A^2 = B^2$.
So $C = B$.

questions.text: A convex lens of focal length $\frac{1}{3}$ m forms a real, inverted image twice the size of the object. The distance of the object from the lens is
questions.explanation:
Real, inverted, twice the size: $v = 2u$ (magnitudes).
Lens formula: $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2u} + \frac{1}{u} = 3$.
$\frac{3}{2u} = 3 \Rightarrow u = 0.5$ m.

questions.text: The frequency of a tuning fork is 256 Hz. It will not resonate with the tuning fork of frequency
questions.explanation:
Resonance occurs at the same frequency or its integral multiples (harmonics): 256, 512, 768, ... Hz.
$754/256$ is not an integer, so 754 Hz will not resonate.

questions.text: A particle carrying a charge equal to 1000 times the charge on an electron, is rotating one rotation per second in a circular path of radius ‘r’ m. If the magnetic field produced at the centre of the path is x times the permeability of vacuum, the radius ‘r’ in m is [$e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C] [$x = 2 \times 10^{-16}$]
questions.explanation:
Equivalent current $I = qf = 1000 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 1 = 1.6 \times 10^{-16}$ A.
$B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2r} = x\mu_0 \Rightarrow r = \frac{I}{2x} = \frac{1.6 \times 10^{-16}}{4 \times 10^{-16}} = 0.4$ m.

questions.text: A particle performing uniform circular motion of radius $\frac{\pi}{2}$ m makes x revolutions in time t. Its tangential velocity is
questions.explanation: $v = 2\pi r \times \frac{x}{t} = 2\pi \times \frac{\pi}{2} \times \frac{x}{t} = \frac{\pi^2 x}{t}$.

questions.text: The frequency of revolution of an electron in the $n^{th}$ orbit of hydrogen atom is
questions.explanation:
$f = \frac{v}{2\pi r}$ with $v \propto \frac{1}{n}$ and $r \propto n^2$.
So $f \propto \frac{1/n}{n^2} = \frac{1}{n^3}$.

questions.text: The initial and final temperatures of water as recorded by an observer are $(38.6 \pm 0.2)$ °C and $(82.3 \pm 0.3)$ °C. The rise in temperature with proper error limits is
questions.explanation:
For a difference, absolute errors add: $\Delta T = 0.2 + 0.3 = 0.5$ °C.
Rise $= 82.3 - 38.6 = 43.7$ °C, so $(43.7 \pm 0.5)$ °C.
Trap: errors never subtract (0.1 is wrong).

questions.text: ‘n’ small water drops of same size (radius r) fall through air with constant velocity V. They coalesce to form a big drop of radius R. The terminal velocity of the big drop is
questions.explanation:
Terminal velocity (Stokes' law): $v = \frac{2r^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{9\eta} \propto r^2$.
So $\frac{V'}{V} = \frac{R^2}{r^2} \Rightarrow V' = \frac{VR^2}{r^2}$.

questions.text: A vertical spring oscillates with period 6 second with mass $m$ is suspended from it. When the mass is at rest, the spring is stretched through a distance of (Take, acceleration due to gravity, $g = \pi^2 = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)
questions.explanation:
At equilibrium $kx = mg \Rightarrow \frac{m}{k} = \frac{x}{g}$, so $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{x}{g}}$.
$x = \frac{gT^2}{4\pi^2} = \frac{\pi^2 \times 36}{4\pi^2} = 9$ m.

questions.text: The electric potential ‘V’ is given as a function of distance ‘x’ (metre) by $V = (4x^2 + 8x - 3)$ V. The value of electric field at $x = 0.5$ m, in V/m is
Out of the following which law obeys the law of conservation of energy?
questions.explanation:
Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change causing it, so mechanical work must be done to produce electrical energy — this is a consequence of conservation of energy.
Trap: Kirchhoff's 1st (junction) law expresses conservation of charge; it is the 2nd (loop) law that relates to energy.

questions.text: In a given logic circuit, the output Y when all the three inputs A, B, C are first low and then high will be respectively
questions.explanation:
The circuit gives $Y = \overline{A} + \overline{B \cdot C}$ (NOT on A, NAND on B, C, then OR).
All low: $\overline{A} = 1 \Rightarrow Y = 1$.
All high: $\overline{A} = 0$, $\overline{1 \cdot 1} = 0 \Rightarrow Y = 0$.
So (1, 0).

questions.text: Two gases A and B are at absolute temperatures 350 K and 420 K respectively. The ratio of average kinetic energy of the molecules of gas B to that of gas A is
questions.explanation:
Average KE per molecule $= \frac{3}{2}kT \propto T$.
$\frac{E_B}{E_A} = \frac{420}{350} = \frac{6}{5}$.

questions.text:
For a particle performing S.H.M. the displacement - time graph is shown.

For that particle the force - time graph is correctly shown
questions.explanation:
From the graph $y = A\sin\omega t$ (starts at 0, rises first).
In SHM $F = -ky = -kA\sin\omega t$: starts at 0 and first goes negative.
That is graph (c). Graph (d) is the displacement shape itself (a common trap).

questions.text: A coil of resistance 450 $\Omega$ and self-inductance 1.5 henry is connected to an a.c. source of frequency $\frac{150}{\pi}$ Hz. The phase difference between voltage and current is
questions.explanation:
$X_L = 2\pi f L = 2\pi \times \frac{150}{\pi} \times 1.5 = 450\ \Omega$.
$\tan\phi = \frac{X_L}{R} = \frac{450}{450} = 1 \Rightarrow \phi = \tan^{-1}(1)$.

questions.text: A small metal sphere of density $\rho$ is dropped from height h into a jar containing liquid of density $\sigma (\sigma > \rho)$. The maximum depth up to which the sphere sinks is (Neglect damping forces)
questions.explanation:
Speed on entering the liquid: $v^2 = 2gh$.
In the liquid, net upward force $= V(\sigma - \rho)g$, so retardation $a = \frac{(\sigma - \rho)g}{\rho}$.
Depth $d = \frac{v^2}{2a} = \frac{h\rho}{\sigma - \rho}$.
The printed options appear misprinted (none shows $\frac{h\rho}{\sigma - \rho}$); (A) is the closest form, $\frac{\rho}{\sigma-\rho}$ times $h$ with the sign reversed.

questions.text: A composite slab consists of two materials having coefficients of thermal conductivity K and 2 K, thickness x and 4x respectively. The temperatures of two outer surfaces of a composite slab are $T_2$ and $T_1$ respectively ($T_2 > T_1$). The rate of heat transfer through the slab in a steady state is $\left[\frac{A(T_2 - T_1)K}{x}\right]f$, where f is equal to
questions.explanation:
Thermal resistances in series: $R = \frac{x}{KA} + \frac{4x}{2KA} = \frac{3x}{KA}$.
Rate $= \frac{T_2 - T_1}{R} = \frac{A(T_2 - T_1)K}{x} \times \frac{1}{3}$.
So $f = \frac{1}{3}$.

questions.text: In an organ pipe closed at one end, the sum of the frequencies of first three overtones is 3930 Hz. The frequency of the fundamental mode of organ pipe is
questions.explanation:
A closed pipe has only odd harmonics; the first three overtones are $3n$, $5n$, $7n$.
$15n = 3930 \Rightarrow n = 262$ Hz.

questions.text: A uniformly charged conducting sphere of diameter 3.5 cm has a surface charge density of 20 $\mu\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$. The total electric flux leaving the surface of the sphere is nearly [permittivity of free space, $\epsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}$ SI unit]
questions.explanation:
$\phi = \frac{q}{\epsilon_0} = \frac{\sigma \cdot 4\pi r^2}{\epsilon_0}$, with $r = 1.75 \times 10^{-2}$ m.
$4\pi r^2 \approx 3.85 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^2}$, $q \approx 7.7 \times 10^{-8}$ C.
$\phi \approx \frac{7.7 \times 10^{-8}}{8.85 \times 10^{-12}} \approx 8.7 \times 10^3$ SI units, closest to $70 \times 10^2$.
(Electric flux is really in $\mathrm{N\,m^2\,C^{-1}}$, not Wb.)

questions.text: A stone is projected with kinetic energy E, making an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. When it reaches a highest point, its kinetic energy is
questions.explanation:
At the highest point only the horizontal velocity $u\cos\theta$ remains.
$KE = \frac{1}{2}m u^2 \cos^2\theta = E\cos^2\theta$.

questions.text: In Young's double slit experiment, the intensity on screen at a point where path difference is $\frac{\lambda}{4}$ is $\frac{K}{2}$. The intensity at a point when path difference is ‘$\lambda$’ will be
questions.explanation:
$I = I_0\cos^2\frac{\phi}{2}$, with $\phi = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x$.
For $\Delta x = \frac{\lambda}{4}$: $\phi = \frac{\pi}{2}$, $I = \frac{I_0}{2} = \frac{K}{2} \Rightarrow I_0 = K$.
For $\Delta x = \lambda$: $\phi = 2\pi$, $I = I_0 = K$.

questions.text: If M is the magnetisation induced in the material, H is the magnetic field intensity, B is the net magnetic field inside the material then the correct relation between them is ($\mu_0$ = permeability of free space)
questions.explanation: The net field inside a magnetised material is $B = \mu_0(H + M)$, where $\mu_0 H$ is the applied part and $\mu_0 M$ is due to magnetisation.

questions.text: Force is applied to a body of mass 3 kg at rest on a frictionless horizontal surface as shown in the force against time (F-t) graph. The speed of the body after 1 s is
questions.explanation:
Impulse = area under F-t graph $= 8 \times 0.5 + 4 \times 0.5 = 6$ N s.
Impulse = change in momentum: $3v = 6 \Rightarrow v = 2$ m/s.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text: An electron accelerated by a potential difference ‘V’ has de-Broglie wavelength ‘$\lambda$’. If the electron is accelerated by a potential difference ‘9V’, its de-Broglie wavelength will be
questions.explanation:
$\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$.
With $9V$: $\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{\sqrt{9}} = \frac{\lambda}{3}$.

questions.text: A weightless thread can bear tension up to 3.7 kg wt. A stone of mass 500 gram is tied to it and revolved in circular path of radius 4 m in vertical plane. Maximum angular velocity of the stone will be (acceleration due to gravity, $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)
questions.explanation:
Tension is maximum at the lowest point: $T = mg + m\omega^2 r$.
$37 = 0.5 \times 10 + 0.5 \times \omega^2 \times 4 \Rightarrow 2\omega^2 = 32$.
$\omega^2 = 16 \Rightarrow \omega = 4$ rad/s.

questions.text: Water is flowing steadily in a river. A and B are the two layers of water at heights 40 cm and 90 cm from the bottom. The velocity of the layer A is 12 cm/s. The velocity of the layer B is
questions.explanation:
In steady (laminar) flow the velocity gradient is uniform, so velocity $\propto$ height from the bottom (bottom layer at rest).
$v_B = 12 \times \frac{90}{40} = 27$ cm/s.

questions.text: A progressive wave of frequency 400 Hz is travelling with velocity 336 m/s. How far apart are the two points on a wave which are 60° out of phase?
questions.explanation:
$\lambda = \frac{v}{f} = \frac{336}{400} = 0.84$ m.
$\Delta x = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi}\Delta\phi = 0.84 \times \frac{60°}{360°} = 0.14$ m.

questions.text: The magnetic flux through a coil is $4 \times 10^{-4}$ Wb at time t = 0. It reduces to 30% of its original value in time t second. If e.m.f. induced in the coil is 0.56 mV then the value of t is
questions.explanation:
Change in flux $= 0.7 \times 4 \times 10^{-4} = 2.8 \times 10^{-4}$ Wb.
$t = \frac{\Delta\phi}{e} = \frac{2.8 \times 10^{-4}}{0.56 \times 10^{-3}} = 0.5$ s.
Trap: using 30% of the flux instead of the 70% decrease.

questions.text: Bohr model is applied to a particle of mass m and charge q is moving in a plane under the influence of a transverse magnetic field (B). The energy of the charged particle in the second level will be (h = Planck's constant)
questions.explanation:
Radius in the field: $r = \frac{mv}{qB}$. Bohr condition: $mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}$.
$\Rightarrow \frac{(mv)^2}{qB} = \frac{nh}{2\pi} \Rightarrow (mv)^2 = \frac{nhqB}{2\pi}$.
Energy (purely kinetic) $E = \frac{(mv)^2}{2m} = \frac{nhqB}{4\pi m}$.
For $n = 2$: $E = \frac{qBh}{2\pi m}$.

questions.text: The co-efficient of absorption and the coefficient of reflection of a thin uniform plate are 0.77 and 0.17 respectively. If 250 kcal of heat is incident on the surface of the plate, the quantity of heat transmitted is
questions.explanation:
$a + r + t = 1 \Rightarrow t = 1 - 0.77 - 0.17 = 0.06$.
Heat transmitted $= 0.06 \times 250 = 15$ kcal.

questions.text: In Fraunhofer diffraction pattern, slit width is 0.2 mm and screen is at 2 m away from the lens. If the distance between the first minimum on either side of the central maximum is 1 cm, the wavelength of light used is
questions.explanation:
Width of central maximum $= \frac{2\lambda D}{a} = 1$ cm.
$\lambda = \frac{0.01 \times 0.2 \times 10^{-3}}{2 \times 2} = 5 \times 10^{-7}$ m $= 5000$ Å.

questions.text: If L is the inductance and R is the resistance then the SI unit of $\frac{L}{R}$ is
questions.explanation:
$\frac{L}{R}$ is the time constant of an LR circuit, so its SI unit is the second.
(Check: henry = $\Omega$ s, so $\frac{\Omega\,s}{\Omega} = $ s.)

questions.text: In an L – R circuit, the inductive reactance is equal to $\sqrt{3}$ times the resistance ‘R’ of the circuit. An e.m.f. $E = E_0 \sin(\omega t)$ is applied to the circuit. The power consumed in the circuit is
A charged particle of mass ‘m’ and charge ‘q’ is at rest. It is accelerated in a uniform electric field of intensity ‘E’ for time ‘t’. The kinetic energy of the particles after time t is
questions.explanation:
$a = \frac{qE}{m}$, so $v = \frac{qEt}{m}$.
$KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{E^2 q^2 t^2}{2m}$.

questions.text: To determine the internal resistance of a cell with potentiometer, when the cell is shunted by a resistance of 5 $\Omega$, the balancing length is 250 cm. When the cell is shunted by 20 $\Omega$, the balancing length of potentiometer wire is 400 cm. The internal resistance of the cell is
questions.explanation:
Terminal voltage $V = \frac{ER}{R + r} \propto l$.
$\frac{250}{400} = \frac{5/(5 + r)}{20/(20 + r)} = \frac{20 + r}{4(5 + r)}$.
$2.5(5 + r) = 20 + r \Rightarrow 12.5 + 2.5r = 20 + r \Rightarrow r = 5\ \Omega$.

questions.text: A body slides down a smooth inclined plane of inclination $\theta$ and reaches the bottom with velocity V. If the same body is a ring which rolls down the same inclined plane then linear velocity at the bottom of plane is
questions.explanation:
Sliding: $V = \sqrt{2gh}$.
Rolling: $v = \sqrt{\frac{2gh}{1 + K^2/R^2}}$; for a ring $K^2/R^2 = 1$, so $v = \sqrt{gh} = \frac{V}{\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.text: Two parallel plate air capacitors of same capacity ‘C’ are connected in parallel to a battery of e.m.f. ‘E’. Then one of the capacitors is completely filled with dielectric material of constant ‘K’. The change in the effective capacity of the parallel combination is
questions.explanation:
Initially $C_{eq} = 2C$. After filling one: $C_{eq} = KC + C$.
Change $= KC + C - 2C = C(K - 1)$.

questions.text: An ideal gas at pressure ‘P’ and temperature ‘T’ is enclosed in a vessel of volume ‘V’. Some gas leaks through a hole from the vessel and the pressure of the enclosed gas falls to ‘P′’. Assuming that the temperature of the gas remains constant during the leakage, the number of moles of the gas that have leaked is
questions.explanation:
$n = \frac{PV}{RT}$ (V, T constant).
Moles leaked $= \frac{PV}{RT} - \frac{P'V}{RT} = \frac{V}{RT}(P - P')$.

questions.text: The escape velocity of a satellite from the surface of earth does NOT depend on

options.text: mass of the object to be projected.

questions.explanation: $v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$ depends on G, M (earth) and R, but not on the mass of the projected object.

questions.text: In unbiased p-n junction diode

options.text: there is an electric field at the junction directed from the p-type side to the n-type side.
there is an electric field at the junction directed from the n-type side to p-type side.
the p-type side is at higher potential than the n-type side.

questions.explanation:
Diffusion leaves positive donor ions on the n-side and negative acceptor ions on the p-side of the depletion region.
So the built-in field points from n-side to p-side, and the n-side is at higher potential.

questions.text: If r.m.s. velocity of hydrogen molecules is 4 times that of an oxygen molecule at 47°C, the temperature of hydrogen molecules is (Molecular weight of Hydrogen and Oxygen are 2 and 32 respectively)
questions.explanation:
$v_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$, so $\frac{v_H^2}{v_O^2} = \frac{T_H/2}{320/32} = 16$.
$\frac{T_H}{20} = 16 \Rightarrow T_H = 320$ K $= 47$ °C.
Trap: use kelvin (47 °C = 320 K).

questions.text: Two cells $E_1$ and $E_2$ having equal e.m.f ‘E’ and internal resistances $r_1$ and $r_2$ ($r_1 > r_2$) respectively are connected in series. This combination is connected to an external resistance ‘R’. It is observed that the potential difference across the cell $E_1$ becomes zero. The value of R will be
questions.explanation:
$I = \frac{2E}{R + r_1 + r_2}$.
PD across $E_1$: $E - Ir_1 = 0 \Rightarrow E = \frac{2Er_1}{R + r_1 + r_2}$.
$R + r_1 + r_2 = 2r_1 \Rightarrow R = r_1 - r_2$.

questions.text: If the length of the oscillating simple pendulum is made $\frac{1}{3}$ times the original keeping amplitude same then increase in its total energy at a place will be
questions.explanation:
Energy of SHM: $E = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2 = \frac{1}{2}m\frac{g}{L}A^2 \propto \frac{1}{L}$ (same amplitude).
$L \to \frac{L}{3} \Rightarrow E \to 3E$, i.e. the energy becomes 3 times.
(Strictly the increase is $2E$, but the intended answer is that energy becomes 3 times.)

questions.text: Two long conductors separated by a distance ‘d’ carry currents ‘$I_1$’ and ‘$I_2$’ in the same directions. They exert a force ‘F’ on each other. The distance between them is increased to ‘3d’. If new repulsive force of magnitude ‘$\frac{2}{3}F$’ is found between these conductors, the required change in the magnitude and direction of one of the currents in the conductor is respectively [length of the conductors is constant]
questions.explanation:
$F \propto \frac{I_1 I_2}{d}$. New: $\frac{I_1 I_2'}{3d} = \frac{2}{3}\frac{I_1 I_2}{d} \Rightarrow I_2' = 2I_2$.
The force changes from attractive (same direction) to repulsive, so the current must be reversed.
Answer: twice, reversed.

questions.text: In a transistor amplifier, AC current gain is 64, the load resistance is 5400 $\Omega$ and the input resistance of the transistor is 540 $\Omega$. The voltage gain is
questions.explanation: $A_v = \beta \frac{R_L}{R_{in}} = 64 \times \frac{5400}{540} = 640$.

questions.text: A monoatomic ideal gas is heated at constant pressure. The percentage of total heat used in increasing the internal energy and that used for doing external work is A and B respectively. Then the ratio, A : B is
questions.explanation:
At constant pressure: $Q = nC_p\Delta T = \frac{5}{2}nR\Delta T$, $\Delta U = \frac{3}{2}nR\Delta T$, $W = nR\Delta T$.
$A : B = \Delta U : W = \frac{3}{2} : 1 = 3 : 2$.

questions.text: An a.c. source is applied to a series LR circuit with $X_L = 3R$ and power factor is $X_1$. Now a capacitor with $X_c = R$ is added in series to LR circuit and the power factor is $X_2$. The ratio $X_1$ to $X_2$ is

When two tuning forks are sounded together, 6 beats per second are heard. One of the fork is in unison with 0.70 m length of sonometer wire and another fork is in unison with 0.69 m length of the same sonometer wire. The frequencies of the two tuning forks are
questions.explanation:
For the same wire and tension, $n \propto \frac{1}{l}$: $0.70\,n_1 = 0.69\,n_2$ with $n_2 = n_1 + 6$.
$0.70n_1 = 0.69n_1 + 4.14 \Rightarrow n_1 = 414$ Hz, $n_2 = 420$ Hz.

questions.text: The maximum velocity of the photoelectrons emitted by a metal surface is $9 \times 10^5$ m/s. The value of ratio of charge (e) to mass (m) of the photoelectron is $1.8 \times 10^{11}$ C/kg. The value of stopping potential in volt is

In Young’s double slit experiment let ‘d’ be the distance between two slits and ‘D’ be the distance between the slits and the screen. Using a monochromatic source of wavelength '$\lambda$', in an interference pattern, third minimum is observed exactly in front of one of the slits. If at the same point on the screen first minimum is to be obtained, the required change in the wavelength is [d & D are not changed]
questions.explanation:
The point in front of a slit is at $y = \frac{d}{2}$ from the centre.
$n^{th}$ minimum: $y = \frac{(2n - 1)\lambda D}{2d}$. Third minimum: $\frac{d}{2} = \frac{5\lambda D}{2d} \Rightarrow d^2 = 5\lambda D$.
First minimum there with $\lambda'$: $\frac{d}{2} = \frac{\lambda' D}{2d} \Rightarrow \lambda' = \frac{d^2}{D} = 5\lambda$.
Required change $= 5\lambda - \lambda = 4\lambda$. (Trap: $5\lambda$ is the new wavelength, not the change.)

questions.text: What is IUPAC name of following compound?
questions.explanation:
The structure is $\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-C(CH_3)_2-Br}$.
Longest chain containing the C=C has 5 carbons (one of the gem-methyls is part of the chain) → pent-2-ene.
Numbering from the end nearer the double bond: C=C at C2, Br and CH₃ on C4.
Name: 4-Bromo-4-methylpent-2-ene.

questions.text: What is the value of $K_{sp}$ for saturated solution of $\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}$ having pH 12?
questions.explanation:
pH = 12 ⇒ pOH = 2 ⇒ $[\mathrm{OH^-}] = 10^{-2}$ M.
$\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2 \rightleftharpoons Ba^{2+} + 2OH^-}$, so $[\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}] = \frac{10^{-2}}{2} = 5 \times 10^{-3}$ M.
$K_{sp} = [\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}][\mathrm{OH^-}]^2 = (5 \times 10^{-3})(10^{-2})^2 = 5 \times 10^{-7}$.

questions.text: Benzonitrile on reduction with stannous chloride in presence of hydrochloric acid followed by acid hydrolysis forms,
questions.explanation:
This is the Stephen reduction: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CN \xrightarrow{SnCl_2/HCl} C_6H_5CH=NH\cdot HCl}$ (imine salt).
Acid hydrolysis of the imine gives $\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}$, benzaldehyde.

questions.text: Identify from following salts so that the solubility of salt in water decreases with increase in temperature.
questions.explanation:
For most salts dissolution is endothermic, so solubility rises with temperature.
$\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}$ is the classic exception: above about 32 °C its solubility decreases as temperature increases (dissolution of the anhydrous salt is exothermic).

questions.text: Which from following polymers is obtained by condensation polymerisation method?
questions.explanation:
Nylon 6,6 is formed from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid with loss of water molecules – a condensation polymer.
Polythene, polyacrylonitrile and Teflon are addition (chain-growth) polymers of alkenes.

questions.text: For a Galvanic cell consisting zinc electrode and standard hydrogen electrode, $E^\circ(\mathrm{Zn^{+2}_{(aq)} \mid Zn_{(s)}}) = 0.76$ V. Identify the reaction that takes place at positive electrode during working of cell?
questions.explanation:
In a galvanic cell the positive electrode is the cathode, where reduction occurs.
Zinc ($E^\circ_{\mathrm{Zn^{2+}/Zn}} = -0.76$ V, i.e. Zn lies below hydrogen) is oxidised at the anode, so the SHE is the cathode.
Cathode reaction: $\mathrm{2H^+_{(aq)} + 2e^- \rightarrow H_{2(g)}}$.
(The question prints the potential without its minus sign; the actual value is −0.76 V.)

questions.text: Which from following polymers is classified as fibre?
questions.explanation:
Fibres have strong intermolecular forces (H-bonding) and high tensile strength; Nylon 6,6 is a typical fibre.
Urea–formaldehyde resin is a thermosetting polymer, polystyrene a thermoplastic, and neoprene an elastomer.

questions.text: Which from following is a correct representation of reaction rate for reaction stated below? $\mathrm{N_{2(g)} + 3H_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2NH_{3(g)}}$
questions.explanation:
Rate = (−1/coefficient)·d[reactant]/dt = (+1/coefficient)·d[product]/dt.
Rate $= -\frac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{3}\frac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{NH_3}]}{dt}$ → option (C).
(Option D is just (C) multiplied by −1, but (C) is the standard way of writing the rate, which must be positive.)

questions.text: Which of the following methods is used to prepare dihydrogen with purity greater than 99.5?
questions.explanation:
Very pure dihydrogen (> 99.5 %) is obtained by electrolysing warm aqueous barium hydroxide solution between nickel electrodes.
Option (D) refers to this method (printed as $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$; the standard text says $\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}$).
Pure water is a poor conductor and cannot be electrolysed directly.

questions.text: Cyclohexene on oxidation with $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ in dil. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ forms.
questions.explanation:
Acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ cleaves the C=C bond; each =CH– carbon becomes –COOH.
Ring opening of cyclohexene gives $\mathrm{HOOC-(CH_2)_4-COOH}$, adipic (hexanedioic) acid.

questions.text: Calculate the enthalpy change of vaporisation of benzene if 13 gram of benzene vaporised by supplying 5.1 kJ of heat.
questions.explanation:
Molar mass of $\mathrm{C_6H_6}$ = 78 g/mol, so moles = $\frac{13}{78} = \frac{1}{6}$ mol.
$\Delta_{vap}H = \frac{5.1}{1/6} = 30.6$ kJ $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$.

questions.text: The volume of simple unit cell is $x \times 10^{-23}$ $\mathrm{cm^3}$. Calculate the value of x if volume occupied by a particle in it is $2.1 \times 10^{-23}$ $\mathrm{cm^3}$.
questions.explanation:
A simple cubic cell contains 1 particle and has packing efficiency 52.4 %.
So volume of particle = 0.524 × volume of cell.
$V_{cell} = \frac{2.1 \times 10^{-23}}{0.524} \approx 4.0 \times 10^{-23}$ $\mathrm{cm^3}$ ⇒ x = 4.0.

questions.text: What is IUPAC name of the following compound?
questions.explanation:
The compound is a cyclobutane ring carrying –OCH₃ on one carbon and two CH₃ groups on the opposite carbon.
Substituent locants are {1,1,3} or {1,3,3}; the lowest set is 1,1,3, so the gem-dimethyl carbon is C1.
Name (prefixes alphabetical): 3-Methoxy-1,1-dimethylcyclobutane.
Trap: (A) gives the higher locant set 1,3,3.

questions.text: What is the pH of buffer solution prepared by mixing 0.01 M weak acid and 0.02 M salt of weak acid with strong base? ($\mathrm{p}K_a$ = 4.680)
questions.explanation:
Henderson equation: $\mathrm{pH} = \mathrm{p}K_a + \log\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{acid}]}$.
$\mathrm{pH} = 4.680 + \log\frac{0.02}{0.01} = 4.680 + 0.301 = 4.981$.

questions.text: Calculate the entropy change of surrounding if 2 moles of $\mathrm{H_2}$ and 1 mole of $\mathrm{O_2}$ gas combine to form 2 moles of liquid water by releasing 525 kJ heat to surrounding at constant pressure and at 300 K.
questions.explanation:
$\Delta S_{surr} = \frac{q_{surr}}{T} = \frac{-\Delta H_{sys}}{T}$.
Heat released to the surroundings = 525 kJ = 525000 J.
$\Delta S_{surr} = \frac{525000}{300} = 1750$ J $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$.

questions.text: Identify the bond line formula of Neopentane.
questions.explanation:
Neopentane is 2,2-dimethylpropane, $\mathrm{C(CH_3)_4}$: one central carbon bonded to four methyl groups.
In bond-line form this is a cross (X) – option (C).
(A) is isopentane (2-methylbutane), (B) is 2,3-dimethylbutane and (D) is n-pentane.

questions.text: What is the number of faraday required to form 1 mol $\mathrm{H_2}$ by reduction of $\mathrm{H^+}$ ions?
questions.explanation:
$\mathrm{2H^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow H_2}$.
1 mol $\mathrm{H_2}$ needs 2 mol electrons = 2 F.

questions.text: Identify the name of method used for three dimensional representation of molecule as follows.
questions.explanation: A cross in which the horizontal bonds point toward the viewer and vertical bonds point away, with the chiral carbon at the intersection, is a Fischer projection (shown here for lactic acid).

questions.text: Identify the correct molecular formula of ‘Oleum’ from following.
questions.explanation:
Oleum (fuming sulphuric acid / pyrosulphuric acid) forms when $\mathrm{SO_3}$ dissolves in $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$:
$\mathrm{SO_3 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow H_2S_2O_7}$.
$\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}$ is peroxodisulphuric acid.

questions.text: Which of the following is a redox reaction?
questions.explanation:
In (D), Zn goes from 0 to +2 (oxidised) and Ag goes from +1 to 0 (reduced) – a redox (displacement) reaction.
(A), (B), (C) are double-decomposition reactions with no change in oxidation states.

questions.text: Identify the product ‘B’ in the following sequence of reactions. Methyl magnesium bromide $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{CdCl_2}}$ A $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{CH_3COCl}}$ B.
questions.explanation:
$\mathrm{2CH_3MgBr + CdCl_2 \rightarrow (CH_3)_2Cd}$ (A) + $\mathrm{2MgBrCl}$.
$\mathrm{(CH_3)_2Cd + 2CH_3COCl \rightarrow 2CH_3COCH_3 + CdCl_2}$.
B = acetone (propanone). A is dimethyl cadmium – the intermediate, not B.

questions.text: What is the number of $>\mathrm{C=C}<$ bonds present in a linolenic acid molecule?
questions.explanation:
Linolenic acid is $\mathrm{C_{17}H_{29}COOH}$ (octadeca-9,12,15-trienoic acid), with three C=C double bonds.
(Oleic acid has one, linoleic acid has two.)

questions.text: Which among the following is an allylic halide?
questions.explanation:
In an allylic halide the halogen is on the sp³ carbon next to a C=C.
3-Bromopropene, $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2Br}$, is allyl bromide.
1- and 2-bromopropene are vinylic halides; in 4-bromobut-1-ene the Br is two carbons away (homoallylic).

questions.text: When tert butyl bromide is heated with silver fluoride the major product obtained is
questions.explanation:
Swarts reaction: the halogen is simply exchanged for F without rearrangement.
$\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-Br + AgF \rightarrow (CH_3)_3C-F + AgBr}$.
tert-Butyl fluoride = 2-fluoro-2-methylpropane.

questions.text: Calculate the molal elevation constant of solvent if boiling point of 0.12 m solution is 319.8 K (Boling point of solvent = 319.5 K)
Which from following pairs of carbohydrates produce equal quantity of glucose on hydrolysis per mole?
questions.explanation:
Glucose obtained per mole on hydrolysis:
Sucrose → glucose + fructose (1 glucose); Lactose → glucose + galactose (1 glucose);
Maltose → 2 glucose; Raffinose → glucose + fructose + galactose (1 glucose).
Only sucrose and lactose give the same amount (1 mol each).

questions.text: Which of the following molecules has a regular geometry as expected?
questions.explanation:
$\mathrm{SiCl_4}$ has 4 bond pairs and no lone pair on Si → regular tetrahedron.
$\mathrm{SF_4}$ (see-saw), $\mathrm{BrF_5}$ (square pyramidal) and $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ (square planar) have lone pairs, so their shapes differ from the regular electron-pair geometry.

questions.text: What is the loss in molar mass when a primary amine is obtained by Hofmann degradation of amide?
questions.explanation:
$\mathrm{RCONH_2 + Br_2 + 4NaOH \rightarrow RNH_2 + Na_2CO_3 + 2NaBr + 2H_2O}$.
The amine has one carbon less: $\mathrm{RCONH_2}$ → $\mathrm{RNH_2}$ removes a CO unit.
Loss in molar mass = 12 + 16 = 28 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$.

questions.text: Which from following is true according to Gay-Lussac’s law ?

options.text: $\frac{V}{T}$ = Constant a costant pressure and for fixed mass of gas.
$\frac{p}{d}$ = constant at constant temperature and fixed mass of gas.
$\frac{P}{T}$ = constant at constant volume and fixed mass of gas.
P × V = constant at constant temperature and for fixed mass of gas.

questions.explanation:
Gay-Lussac’s (pressure–temperature) law: at constant volume, the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to absolute temperature, i.e. $\frac{P}{T}$ = constant.
(A) is Charles’ law and (D) is Boyle’s law.

questions.text: Identify example of sorption from following.

options.text: Charcol is added to methylene blue solution.
Hydrogen gas is passed over platinum
Oxygen gas is passed over finely divided nickel.

questions.explanation:
Sorption = adsorption and absorption occurring together.
When chalk is dipped in ink, the colouring matter is adsorbed on the surface while the solvent is absorbed into the bulk – sorption.
Charcoal + methylene blue is pure adsorption.

questions.text: Which from following carbohydrates produces double quantity of glucose on hydrolysis per mole as compared with sucrose?
questions.explanation:
Sucrose gives 1 mol glucose (+ 1 mol fructose) per mole.
Maltose (glucose–glucose) gives 2 mol glucose – double.
Lactose, raffinose and stachyose each contain only one glucose unit.

questions.text: In ionic solid, anions are arranged in ccp array and cations occupy 1/3 tetrahedral voids. What is the formula of ionic compound? [Consider A = cation; B = anion]
questions.explanation:
If there are N anions (B) in ccp, there are 2N tetrahedral voids.
Cations (A) = $\frac{1}{3} \times 2N = \frac{2N}{3}$.
A : B = $\frac{2}{3}$ : 1 = 2 : 3 ⇒ $\mathrm{A_2B_3}$.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT dihydric alcohol?
questions.explanation:
Catechol (1,2-), resorcinol (1,3-) and hydroquinone (1,4-dihydroxybenzene) each have two –OH groups.
Phloroglucinol is 1,3,5-trihydroxybenzene – trihydric.

questions.text: Calculate the concentration of an aqueous solution of non electrolyte at 300 K if its osmotic pressure is 12 atm. [R= 0.0821 atm $\mathrm{dm^3}$ $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$ $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$]
Which from following compounds is least soluble in water at STP?
questions.explanation:
Ethanol, methanol and methylamine are polar and form hydrogen bonds with water, so they are highly soluble.
$\mathrm{CH_4}$ is non-polar and cannot H-bond with water – least soluble.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct about $\mathrm{O_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_3}$ molecule?

options.text: The enthalpy change during the formation of $\mathrm{O_3}$ from $\mathrm{O_2}$ is positive
The entropy change in the formation of $\mathrm{O_3}$ from $\mathrm{O_2}$ is positive

questions.explanation:
$\mathrm{3O_2 \rightarrow 2O_3}$, $\Delta H \approx +142$ kJ $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$ – endothermic, so (B) is correct.
Gas moles decrease (3 → 2), so $\Delta S$ is negative (C wrong); hence $\mathrm{O_3}$ is less stable than $\mathrm{O_2}$ (D wrong).
$\mathrm{O_2}$ is paramagnetic but $\mathrm{O_3}$ is diamagnetic (A wrong).

questions.text: What is the total number of donor atoms present in Tetracyanonickelate(II) ion?
questions.explanation:
Tetracyanonickelate(II) is $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$.
Each $\mathrm{CN^-}$ is monodentate (binds through C), so there are 4 donor atoms (coordination number 4).

questions.text: Half life of a first order reaction is 900 minute at 400 K, find its half life at 300 K? $\left(\frac{E_a}{2.303R} = 1.3056 \times 10^3\right)$
Which solvent from following is used in order to avoid creation of waste and pollution of air?
questions.explanation:
Green chemistry recommends replacing toxic, volatile chlorinated solvents with safe solvents.
Water is non-toxic, non-flammable and non-polluting – the ideal green solvent.

questions.text: For the cell, $\ominus\mathrm{Zn_{(s)}|Zn^{+2}(1M)||Ag^{+1}(1M)|Ag_{(s)}}\oplus$ If concentration of $\mathrm{Zn^{+2}}$ decreases to 0.1 M at 298 K. then emf of cell
questions.explanation:
Cell reaction: $\mathrm{Zn + 2Ag^+ \rightarrow Zn^{2+} + 2Ag}$, n = 2.
$E = E^\circ - \frac{0.0592}{2}\log\frac{[\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}]}{[\mathrm{Ag^+}]^2}$.
At 1 M, E = E°. With $[\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}] = 0.1$ M: $E = E^\circ - 0.0296 \times (-1) = E^\circ + 0.0296$ V.
So emf increases by 0.0296 V.

questions.text: Identify the product ‘B’ in the following series of reactions. Chlorobenzene $\xrightarrow[\text{ii) } \mathrm{H_3O^+}]{\text{i) NaOH, 623 K/150 atm}}$ A $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2}\text{ water}}$ B
questions.explanation:
Dow process: chlorobenzene + NaOH (623 K, 150 atm), then acidification → phenol (A).
Phenol with bromine water (polar solvent) undergoes trisubstitution → 2,4,6-tribromophenol (white ppt) (B).
Monobromophenols form only with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ in a non-polar solvent such as $\mathrm{CS_2}$.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding voids in lattice structure?

options.text: Four spheres are involved in the formation of a tetrahedral void.
The octahedral void is surrounded by six spheres.
There are two tetrahedral voids associated with each atom.
There is one octahedral void associated with two atoms.

questions.explanation:
In close packing of N spheres: tetrahedral voids = 2N, octahedral voids = N.
So there is one octahedral void per atom, not per two atoms – (D) is incorrect.
(A), (B), (C) are all correct statements.

questions.text: Identify pair of complexes that exhibits solvate isomerism.
questions.explanation:
Solvate (hydrate) isomers differ in whether solvent (water) molecules are coordinated ligands or lattice molecules – pair (A).
(B) ionisation isomers, (C) coordination isomers, (D) linkage isomers.

questions.text: Identify the element from following such that the last electron is placed in $(n-1)$ d orbital.
questions.explanation:
Elements whose differentiating (last) electron enters the $(n-1)d$ subshell are d-block elements.
Ag ($\mathrm{[Kr]4d^{10}5s^1}$) is a d-block element.
Dy, Pu and Pa are f-block elements (lanthanide/actinides), where the last electron enters $(n-2)f$.

questions.text: Which transition series includes elements Co and Mo respectively?
questions.explanation:
Co (Z = 27) is in period 4 → 3d series.
Mo (Z = 42) is in period 5 → 4d series.

questions.text: Rate law for the reaction, $\mathrm{C_2H_5I_{(g)} \rightarrow C_2H_{4(g)} + HI_{(g)}}$ is $r = k[\mathrm{C_2H_5}]$ What is the order and molecularity of this reaction?
questions.explanation:
The rate depends on the first power of one concentration ⇒ first order.
It is an elementary decomposition of a single $\mathrm{C_2H_5I}$ molecule ⇒ unimolecular (molecularity 1).
(The rate law should read $k[\mathrm{C_2H_5I}]$.)

questions.text: Find the mass of potassium chloride required to liberate 5.6 $\mathrm{dm^3}$ of oxygen gas at STP? (molar mass of $\mathrm{KClO_3}$ = 122.5 g/mol)
questions.explanation:
$\mathrm{2KClO_3 \rightarrow 2KCl + 3O_2}$ (the substance heated is potassium chlorate, as the given molar mass shows).
Moles of $\mathrm{O_2} = \frac{5.6}{22.4} = 0.25$ mol.
Moles of $\mathrm{KClO_3} = \frac{2}{3} \times 0.25 = \frac{1}{6}$ mol.
Mass = $\frac{122.5}{6} \approx 20.4$ g.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions exhibits decrease in entropy?
questions.explanation:
Entropy decreases when the number of gas moles decreases or gas turns to liquid/solid.
In (D), 3 mol of gas form 2 mol of liquid water → $\Delta S < 0$.
(A), (B), (C) all produce gas molecules → $\Delta S > 0$.

questions.text: What is the wavenumber of the photon emitted during transition from the orbit n = 5 to that of n = 2 in hydrogen atom? [$R_H$ = 109677 $\mathrm{cm^{-1}}$]
questions.explanation:
$\bar{\nu} = R_H\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right) = 109677\left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{25}\right)$.
$= 109677 \times \frac{21}{100} \approx 23032$ $\mathrm{cm^{-1}}$.

questions.text: If pH of solution changes from 4 to 5. then the $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ ion concentration of solution
questions.explanation:
$[\mathrm{H_3O^+}] = 10^{-\mathrm{pH}}$.
pH 4 → $10^{-4}$ M; pH 5 → $10^{-5}$ M.
The concentration decreases by a factor of 10 (each unit rise in pH = 10-fold decrease).

questions.text: The last column in the truth table of the statement pattern $[p \to (q \wedge \sim p)] \vee [(p \vee \sim q) \wedge p]$ is
questions.explanation:
Rows in order $(p,q)$: TT, TF, FT, FF.
$q \wedge \sim p$: F, F, T, F, so $p \to (q \wedge \sim p)$: F, F, T, T.
$(p \vee \sim q) \wedge p$ is true exactly when $p$ is T: T, T, F, F.
OR of the two columns: T, T, T, T (a tautology).

questions.text: A straight line through the origin O meets the line $3y = 10 - 4x$ and $8x + 6y + 5 = 0$ at the points A and B respectively. Then O divides the segment AB in the ratio.
questions.explanation:
The lines $4x + 3y - 10 = 0$ and $4x + 3y + \frac{5}{2} = 0$ are parallel, and O lies between them (opposite signs at O).
Distance of O from first line $= \frac{10}{5} = 2$; from second $= \frac{5/2}{5} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Any line through O cuts them so that $OA : OB = 2 : \frac{1}{2} = 4 : 1$.

questions.text: The position of a point in time t is given by $x = a + bt^2 - ct^2$, $y = at + bt^2$. It's resultant acceleration at time t in seconds is given by
questions.explanation:
The intended (standard) question is $x = a + bt - ct^2$, $y = at + bt^2$.
Then $\ddot{x} = -2c$ and $\ddot{y} = 2b$.
Resultant acceleration $= \sqrt{(-2c)^2 + (2b)^2} = 2\sqrt{b^2 + c^2}$.
(With $x$ exactly as printed, $\ddot{x} = 2b - 2c$, giving $2\sqrt{(b-c)^2 + b^2}$, which is not an option.)

questions.text: Let $\overline{OA} = \bar{a}$, $\overline{OB} = \bar{b}$ and if the vector along the angle bisector of $\angle AOB$ is given by $x\frac{\bar{a}}{|\bar{a}|} + y\frac{\bar{b}}{|\bar{b}|}$ then
questions.explanation:
The internal bisector of $\angle AOB$ is along the sum of unit vectors: $\lambda\left(\frac{\bar{a}}{|\bar{a}|} + \frac{\bar{b}}{|\bar{b}|}\right)$.
So the two coefficients are equal: $x = y$, i.e. $x - y = 0$.

questions.text: In triangle ABC, the point P divides BC internally in the ratio $3 : 4$ and Q divides CA internally in the ratio $5 : 3$. If AP and BQ intersect in a point G, then G divides AP internally in the ratio
questions.explanation:
$\bar{p} = \frac{4\bar{b} + 3\bar{c}}{7}$, $\bar{q} = \frac{5\bar{a} + 3\bar{c}}{8}$.
On AP: $\bar{g} = (1-s)\bar{a} + \frac{4s}{7}\bar{b} + \frac{3s}{7}\bar{c}$; on BQ: $\bar{g} = \frac{5t}{8}\bar{a} + (1-t)\bar{b} + \frac{3t}{8}\bar{c}$.
Comparing: $t = \frac{8s}{7}$ and $\frac{4s}{7} = 1 - \frac{8s}{7} \Rightarrow s = \frac{7}{12}$.
So $AG : GP = s : (1-s) = 7 : 5$.

questions.text: The derivative of $y = (1 - x)(2 - x) \ldots (n - x)$ at $x = 1$ is
questions.explanation:
By the product rule, every term except the one where $(1 - x)$ is differentiated contains the factor $(1 - x)$, which is 0 at $x = 1$.
So $y'(1) = (-1)\cdot(2-1)(3-1)\cdots(n-1) = (-1)(n-1)!$.

questions.text: If $X \sim B(n, p)$ then $\frac{P(X=k)}{P(X=k-1)} =$
questions.explanation:
$\frac{P(X=k)}{P(X=k-1)} = \frac{\binom{n}{k}p^k q^{n-k}}{\binom{n}{k-1}p^{k-1}q^{n-k+1}} = \frac{\binom{n}{k}}{\binom{n}{k-1}}\cdot\frac{p}{q}$.
And $\frac{\binom{n}{k}}{\binom{n}{k-1}} = \frac{n-k+1}{k}$.

questions.text: The differential equation of all straight lines passing through the point $(1, -1)$ is
questions.explanation:
Lines through $(1, -1)$: $y + 1 = m(x - 1)$.
Differentiating, $m = \frac{dy}{dx}$.
Eliminating $m$: $y = (x - 1)\frac{dy}{dx} - 1$.

questions.text: The first derivative of the function $\left(\cos^{-1}\left(\sin\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{2}}\right) + x^x\right)$ with respect to $x$ at $x = 1$ is
questions.explanation:
Let $u = \sqrt{\frac{1+x}{2}}$ (near $x=1$, $u \approx 1$ rad). Then $\cos^{-1}(\sin u) = \frac{\pi}{2} - u$, whose derivative is $-u'$.
$u' = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1+x}{2}\right)^{-1/2}\cdot\frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}$ at $x = 1$.
$\frac{d}{dx}x^x = x^x(1 + \ln x) = 1$ at $x = 1$.
Total $= -\frac{1}{4} + 1 = \frac{3}{4}$.

questions.text: Let $\bar{u}, \bar{v}, \bar{w}$ be the vectors such that $|\bar{u}| = 1, |\bar{v}| = 2, |\bar{w}| = 3$. If the projection $\bar{v}$ along $\bar{u}$ is equal to that of $\bar{w}$ along $\bar{u}$ and the vectors $\bar{v}, \bar{w}$ are perpendicular to each other then $|\bar{u} - \bar{v} + \bar{w}|$ equals
questions.explanation:
Given $\bar{v}\cdot\bar{u} = \bar{w}\cdot\bar{u}$ (since $|\bar{u}| = 1$) and $\bar{v}\cdot\bar{w} = 0$.
$|\bar{u} - \bar{v} + \bar{w}|^2 = 1 + 4 + 9 - 2\bar{u}\cdot\bar{v} + 2\bar{u}\cdot\bar{w} - 2\bar{v}\cdot\bar{w} = 14$.
So the magnitude is $\sqrt{14}$.

questions.text: The area enclosed between the curves $y^2 = 4x$ and $y = |x|$ is
questions.explanation:
$y^2 = 4x$ needs $x \ge 0$, where $y = |x| = x$. Intersections: $x^2 = 4x \Rightarrow x = 0, 4$.
Area $= \int_0^4 (2\sqrt{x} - x)\,dx = \left[\frac{4}{3}x^{3/2} - \frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^4 = \frac{32}{3} - 8 = \frac{8}{3}$.

questions.text: If $\tan A = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x(x^2+x+1)}}$, $\tan B = \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}}$ and $\tan C = \sqrt{x^{-1} + x^{-2} + x^{-3}}$ then

Let X be a discrete random variable. The probability distribution of X is given below
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline X & 30 & 10 & -10 \\ \hline P(X) & \frac{1}{5} & A & B \\ \hline\end{array}$$
and $E(X) = 4$, then the value of AB is equal to
questions.explanation:
Total probability: $\frac{1}{5} + A + B = 1 \Rightarrow A + B = \frac{4}{5}$.
$E(X) = 6 + 10A - 10B = 4 \Rightarrow A - B = -\frac{1}{5}$.
So $A = \frac{3}{10}$, $B = \frac{1}{2}$ and $AB = \frac{3}{20}$.

questions.text: The projection of the line segment joining the points $(2, 1, -3)$ and $(-1, 0, 2)$ on the line whose direction ratios are 3, 2, 6 is
questions.explanation:
Segment vector $= (-3, -1, 5)$; direction cosines $= \left(\frac{3}{7}, \frac{2}{7}, \frac{6}{7}\right)$.
Projection $= \frac{-9 - 2 + 30}{7} = \frac{19}{7}$ units.

questions.text: If $x^{\frac{2}{5}} + y^{\frac{2}{5}} = a^{\frac{2}{5}}$ then $\frac{dy}{dx} =$
questions.explanation:
Differentiate: $\frac{2}{5}x^{-3/5} + \frac{2}{5}y^{-3/5}\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$.
$\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{y^{3/5}}{x^{3/5}} = -\sqrt[5]{\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^3}$.

questions.text: The perpendicular distance between the lines given by $(x - 2y + 1)^2 + k(x - 2y + 1) = 0$ is $\sqrt{5}$, then $k =$
questions.explanation:
Factor: $(x - 2y + 1)(x - 2y + 1 + k) = 0$, two parallel lines.
Distance $= \frac{|k|}{\sqrt{1 + 4}} = \sqrt{5} \Rightarrow |k| = 5$, so $k = 5$.

questions.text: The value of $\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + \cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) - \cot^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + \tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3})$
questions.explanation:
Principal values: $\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{4}$, $\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}$, $\cot^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}$, $\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = -\frac{\pi}{3}$.
As printed the sum is $-\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\pi}{3} = -\frac{7\pi}{12}$, which is not an option.
The intended version (last term $+\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3} = \frac{\pi}{3}$) gives $-\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{12}$, so the best choice is $\frac{\pi}{12}$.

questions.text: If triangle ABC is a right angled at A and $\tan\frac{B}{2}, \tan\frac{C}{2}$ are roots of the equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$, $a \ne 0$, then
questions.explanation:
$A = 90^\circ \Rightarrow \frac{B}{2} + \frac{C}{2} = 45^\circ$, so $\tan\left(\frac{B}{2} + \frac{C}{2}\right) = 1$.
With sum of roots $-\frac{b}{a}$ and product $\frac{c}{a}$: $\frac{-b/a}{1 - c/a} = 1 \Rightarrow -b = a - c$.
Hence $a + b = c$.

questions.text: If $a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = r^2$, then the value of $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{ab}{cr}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{bc}{ar}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{ca}{br}\right) =$
questions.explanation:
Let $x = \frac{ab}{cr}$, $y = \frac{bc}{ar}$, $z = \frac{ca}{br}$. Then $xy = \frac{b^2}{r^2}$, $yz = \frac{c^2}{r^2}$, $zx = \frac{a^2}{r^2}$.
So $xy + yz + zx = \frac{a^2+b^2+c^2}{r^2} = 1$.
When $xy + yz + zx = 1$ (positive $x, y, z$), $\tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}y + \tan^{-1}z = \frac{\pi}{2}$.

questions.text: The value of $\int_{\frac{1}{3}}^{1} (x - x^3)^{\frac{1}{3}}\,dx$ is
questions.explanation:
The standard (intended) integral is $\int_{1/3}^{1} \frac{(x - x^3)^{1/3}}{x^4}\,dx$; the $x^4$ denominator seems to be missing from the print.
Write $\frac{(x - x^3)^{1/3}}{x^4} = \frac{1}{x^3}\left(\frac{1}{x^2} - 1\right)^{1/3}$. Put $t = \frac{1}{x^2} - 1$, $dt = -\frac{2}{x^3}dx$.
Limits: $x = \frac{1}{3} \to t = 8$, $x = 1 \to t = 0$.
Integral $= \frac{1}{2}\int_0^8 t^{1/3}\,dt = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\cdot 8^{4/3} = \frac{3}{8}\cdot 16 = 6$.

questions.text: The feasible region for the constraints $x - 2 \le y$, $x \ge y - 1$, $x \ge 2$, $y \le 4$, $x, y \ge 0$, is ....
questions.explanation:
$x - 2 \le y$: on or above $y = x - 2$. $x \ge y - 1$: on or below $y = x + 1$.
$x \ge 2$: right of $X = 2$; $y \le 4$: below $Y = 4$; and $y \ge 0$.
The common region is the quadrilateral with vertices $(2, 0), (2, 3), (3, 4), (6, 4)$, to the right of $X = 2$ between the two slanted lines, which is the shading in (B).

In a game, 3 coins are tossed. A person is paid ₹150 if he gets all heads or all tails and he is supposed to pay ₹50 if he gets one head or two heads. The amount he can expect to win / lose on an average per game in ₹ is
questions.explanation:
P(all heads or all tails) $= \frac{2}{8} = \frac{1}{4}$; P(one or two heads) $= \frac{3}{4}$.

questions.text: If $\sin\left(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{5} + \cos^{-1}x\right) = 1$, then the value of $x$ is
questions.explanation:
$\sin\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \sin^{-1}\frac{1}{5} + \cos^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{2}$.
Since $\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{5} + \cos^{-1}\frac{1}{5} = \frac{\pi}{2}$, we get $x = \frac{1}{5}$.

questions.text: If two sides of a triangle are $\sqrt{3} - 2$ and $\sqrt{3} + 2$ units and their included angle is $60^\circ$, then the third side of the triangle is
questions.explanation:
Cosine rule: $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos 60^\circ = a^2 + b^2 - ab$.
$a^2 + b^2 = (7 - 4\sqrt{3}) + (7 + 4\sqrt{3}) = 14$, $ab = 3 - 4 = -1$.
$c^2 = 14 + 1 = 15 \Rightarrow c = \sqrt{15}$ units.

questions.text: The principal increases continuously in a newly opened bank at the rate of 10% per year. An amount of Rs. 2000 is deposited with this bank. How much will it become after 5 years? $(e^{0.5} = 1.648)$
questions.explanation:
$\frac{dP}{dt} = 0.1P \Rightarrow P = P_0e^{0.1t}$.
After 5 years: $P = 2000e^{0.5} = 2000 \times 1.648 = 3296$.

questions.text: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $A^{-1} = \alpha I + \beta A$, $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$ where I is the identity matrix of order 2, then $4(\alpha + \beta) =$
questions.explanation:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, $A^2 - (\mathrm{tr}A)A + |A|I = 0$: $\mathrm{tr}A = 5$, $|A| = 4 + 2 = 6$.
$A^2 - 5A + 6I = 0 \Rightarrow A - 5I + 6A^{-1} = 0 \Rightarrow A^{-1} = \frac{5}{6}I - \frac{1}{6}A$.
$4(\alpha + \beta) = 4\left(\frac{5}{6} - \frac{1}{6}\right) = \frac{8}{3}$.

questions.text: Which of the following are pairs of equivalent circuits
questions.explanation:
I: $(S_1 \wedge S_2) \vee (S_1 \wedge S_3) \equiv S_1 \wedge (S_2 \vee S_3)$.
II: $S_1 \vee (S_2 \wedge S_3)$.
III: $S_1 \wedge (S_2 \vee S_3)$.
IV: $S_1 \wedge S_2 \wedge S_3$. V: $(S_1 \wedge S_2) \vee S_3$.
I and III are equivalent (distributive law).

questions.text: The solution of $\frac{dy}{dx} = (x + y)^2$ is

options.text: $\tan^{-1}(x + y) = x + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$x + y = \tan x + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$x + y = \cot^{-1}x + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$x + y = \sin^{-1}(x + y) + c$, where c is the constant of integration

questions.explanation:
Put $v = x + y$: $\frac{dv}{dx} = 1 + \frac{dy}{dx} = 1 + v^2$.
$\int\frac{dv}{1 + v^2} = \int dx \Rightarrow \tan^{-1}(x + y) = x + c$.

questions.text: The equation of the plane passing through the line of intersection of the planes $x + y + z = 1$ and $3x + 4y + 5z = 2$ and perpendicular to the XY-plane is
questions.explanation:
Plane: $(x + y + z - 1) + \lambda(3x + 4y + 5z - 2) = 0$.
Perpendicular to the XY-plane means the $z$-coefficient is 0: $1 + 5\lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = -\frac{1}{5}$.
$5(x + y + z - 1) - (3x + 4y + 5z - 2) = 0 \Rightarrow 2x + y - 3 = 0$.

questions.text: A normal is drawn at a point $P(x, y)$ of a curve $y = f(x)$. The normal meets the X axis at Q. $l(PQ) = k$. (k is a constant) Then equation of the curve through $(0, k)$ is
questions.explanation:
Length of normal $= |y|\sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2} = k$.
This is satisfied by circles $(x - c)^2 + y^2 = k^2$ (the normal passes through the centre on the X-axis, so PQ = radius).
Through $(0, k)$: $c^2 + k^2 = k^2 \Rightarrow c = 0$, so $x^2 + y^2 = k^2$.

questions.text: If $f(x) = \frac{(27 - 2x)^{\frac{1}{3}} - 3}{9 - 3(243 + 5x)^{\frac{1}{5}}}$, $x \ne 0$ is continuous at $x = 0$, then the value of $f(0)$ is

questions.explanation:
For $x \ne 0$, divide by $|x|$ (note $x^2 = |x|^2$): $\frac{1}{1 + |x|}$.
As $x \to 0$, this tends to 1 (from both sides).

questions.text: The value of $\int_{-3}^{3}\sin^7 x\cos^{16}x\,dx$ is
questions.explanation:
$f(x) = \sin^7 x\cos^{16}x$ satisfies $f(-x) = -f(x)$ (odd power of sine).
The integral of an odd function over $[-a, a]$ is 0.

The domain of the function $f(x) = {}^{7-x}P_{x-1}$
questions.explanation:

Domain $= \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$.

questions.text: $\int\frac{x + \sin x}{1 + \cos x}\,dx =$

options.text: $x\cos x + c$, where c is the constant integration
$x\tan x + c$, where c is the constant integration
$x\tan\frac{x}{2} + c$, where c is the constant integration
$x\sec^2\frac{x}{2} + c$, where c is the constant integration

questions.explanation:
$\frac{x + \sin x}{1 + \cos x} = \frac{x}{2}\sec^2\frac{x}{2} + \tan\frac{x}{2}$.
Since $\frac{d}{dx}\left(x\tan\frac{x}{2}\right) = \tan\frac{x}{2} + \frac{x}{2}\sec^2\frac{x}{2}$, the integral is $x\tan\frac{x}{2} + c$.

questions.text: If $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are three vectors such that $|\bar{a}| = 3$, $|\bar{b}| = 5$, $|\bar{c}| = 7$ then $|\bar{a} - \bar{b}|^2 + |\bar{b} - \bar{c}|^2 + |\bar{c} - \bar{a}|^2$ does not exceed
questions.explanation:
Sum $= 2(|\bar{a}|^2 + |\bar{b}|^2 + |\bar{c}|^2) - 2(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{b} + \bar{b}\cdot\bar{c} + \bar{c}\cdot\bar{a})$.
$|\bar{a} + \bar{b} + \bar{c}|^2 \ge 0 \Rightarrow 2(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{b} + \bar{b}\cdot\bar{c} + \bar{c}\cdot\bar{a}) \ge -83$.
So Sum $= 3(83) - |\bar{a} + \bar{b} + \bar{c}|^2 \le 249$.

questions.text: Total number of 3-digit numbers, whose g.c.d with 36 is 2, is
questions.explanation:
$36 = 2^2\cdot 3^2$. gcd $= 2$ means $n = 2m$ with $m$ odd and $3 \nmid m$.
$100 \le n \le 999 \Rightarrow 50 \le m \le 499$: odd $m$ from 51 to 499: 225 numbers.
Odd multiples of 3 in that range (51, 57, ..., 495): 75.
Count $= 225 - 75 = 150$.

questions.text: If $\frac{z - 1}{2z + 1}$ is an imaginary number and if it represents a circle then its radius is
questions.explanation:
Purely imaginary means $\mathrm{Re}\left[(z - 1)(2\bar{z} + 1)\right] = 0$. With $z = x + iy$:
$(x - 1)(2x + 1) + 2y^2 = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 + y^2 - \frac{x}{2} - \frac{1}{2} = 0$.
Radius $= \sqrt{\frac{1}{16} + \frac{1}{2}} = \frac{3}{4}$ units.

questions.text: If $\int\tan^4 x\,dx = a\tan^3 x + b\tan x + cx + k$ (where k is the constant of integration) then the value of $a - b + c =$
questions.explanation:
$\tan^4 x = \tan^2 x\sec^2 x - \sec^2 x + 1$.
$\int\tan^4 x\,dx = \frac{\tan^3 x}{3} - \tan x + x + k$.
$a = \frac{1}{3}$, $b = -1$, $c = 1 \Rightarrow a - b + c = \frac{7}{3}$.

questions.text: The lines $\frac{x - 3}{1} = \frac{y - 2}{1} = \frac{z - 5}{-k}$ and $\frac{x - 4}{k} = \frac{y - 3}{1} = \frac{z - 3}{2}$ are coplanar, hence $k =$

$\log\left(\frac{x-2}{(x-1)^2}\right) + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$\log\left(\frac{x-2}{x-1}\right) + c$, where $c$ is the constant of integration
$\log\left(\frac{(x-2)^2}{x-1}\right) + c$, where c is the constant of integration

questions.explanation:
Partial fractions: $\frac{x}{(x-1)(x-2)} = \frac{-1}{x - 1} + \frac{2}{x - 2}$.
Integral $= 2\log|x - 2| - \log|x - 1| + c = \log\left(\frac{(x-2)^2}{x-1}\right) + c$.

questions.text: Let A and B are independent events with $P(B) = \frac{2}{5}$, $P(A \cup B) = \frac{11}{20}$, then $P(A'|B)$ is root of the equation
questions.explanation:
Independent: $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A)P(B) = \frac{2}{5} + \frac{3}{5}P(A) = \frac{11}{20} \Rightarrow P(A) = \frac{1}{4}$.
$P(A'|B) = P(A') = \frac{3}{4}$.
Check: $4\cdot\frac{9}{16} - 7\cdot\frac{3}{4} + 3 = \frac{9 - 21 + 12}{4} = 0$. ✓

questions.text: The equation of tangent to the curve $y = \cos(x + y)$ where $-2\pi \le x \le 2\pi$ and which is parallel to the line $x + 2y = 0$, is
questions.explanation:
$y' = -\sin(x + y)(1 + y') \Rightarrow y' = \frac{-\sin(x+y)}{1 + \sin(x+y)}$.
Slope $-\frac{1}{2}$ gives $\sin(x + y) = 1$, so $y = \cos(x + y) = 0$ and $x = \frac{\pi}{2}$ or $-\frac{3\pi}{2}$.
At $\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right)$: $y = -\frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \Rightarrow 2x + 4y - \pi = 0$.
(The other point gives $2x + 4y + 3\pi = 0$, not listed.)

questions.text: The eccentricity of the ellipse $9x^2 + 5y^2 - 30y = 0$ is
questions.explanation:
$9x^2 + 5(y - 3)^2 = 45 \Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{5} + \frac{(y-3)^2}{9} = 1$ (major axis vertical).
$e^2 = 1 - \frac{5}{9} = \frac{4}{9} \Rightarrow e = \frac{2}{3}$.

questions.text: If the tangent at $(1, 7)$ to the curve $x^2 = y - 6$ touches the circle $x^2 + y^2 + 16x + 12y + C = 0$, then $C =$
questions.explanation:
$y = x^2 + 6 \Rightarrow y' = 2$ at $x = 1$. Tangent: $y = 2x + 5$, i.e. $2x - y + 5 = 0$.
Circle: centre $(-8, -6)$, radius $\sqrt{100 - C}$.
Distance $= \frac{|-16 + 6 + 5|}{\sqrt{5}} = \sqrt{5} \Rightarrow 100 - C = 5 \Rightarrow C = 95$.

questions.text: The value of 'a' so that the sum of squares of the roots of the equation $x^2 - (a - 2)x - a + 1 = 0$ assumes the least value is
questions.explanation:
$\alpha + \beta = a - 2$, $\alpha\beta = 1 - a$.
$\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (a - 2)^2 - 2(1 - a) = a^2 - 2a + 2 = (a - 1)^2 + 1$.
Least when $a = 1$.

questions.text: If the shortest distance between the lines $\bar{r}_1 = \alpha\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k} + \lambda(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$, $\alpha > 0$ and $\bar{r}_2 = -4\hat{i} - \hat{k} + \mu(3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$, $\mu \in \mathbb{R}$, is 9, then the value of $\alpha$ is
questions.explanation:
$\bar{b}_1 \times \bar{b}_2 = (1, -2, 2) \times (3, -2, -2) = (8, 8, 4)$, magnitude 12.
$\bar{a}_2 - \bar{a}_1 = (-4 - \alpha, -2, -3)$; dot product $= -32 - 8\alpha - 16 - 12 = -60 - 8\alpha$.
$\frac{|60 + 8\alpha|}{12} = 9 \Rightarrow 60 + 8\alpha = 108 \Rightarrow \alpha = 6$ (taking $\alpha > 0$).

questions.text: If two curves $x^2 - 4y^2 = 2$ and $8x^2 = 40 - my^2$ are orthogonal to each other then $m =$
questions.explanation:
For $\frac{x^2}{A_1} + \frac{y^2}{B_1} = 1$ and $\frac{x^2}{A_2} + \frac{y^2}{B_2} = 1$ to cut orthogonally: $A_1 - B_1 = A_2 - B_2$.
First: $\frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{y^2}{1/2} = 1$: $A_1 - B_1 = 2 + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{2}$.
Second: $\frac{x^2}{5} + \frac{y^2}{40/m} = 1$: $5 - \frac{40}{m} = \frac{5}{2} \Rightarrow m = 16$.
